tasks.short: Estimate consumption, then requisition, purchase, or draw from storage.

steps.what: Read bookings before the estimate of expected consumption
Draft a requisition from par levels and expected consumption
Count food in storage against the requisition
Decide what to purchase and what to procure from storage
Send the purchase of supplies or the store requisition

tasks.design: Bookings in {CALENDAR} and par levels in {ERP} draft a requisition from expected consumption. The cook still counts storage and still decides what to purchase or procure. The order leaves through {PROCUREMENT} only after that decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Covers, waste and a special are known in the kitchen, and the shelf is the only count that matches them.
tasks.enabler_now: A booking list and a par level can propose quantities. The proposal is arithmetic, and the cook still changes it after the count.
tasks.still_hard: A walk-in service and a spoiled tray are not in the booking list, so the shelf count stays.
tasks.human_edge: Seeing what is actually in storage, and refusing a suggested line the service will not use.

ambition.what: Whether a short-life item is ordered before the supplier cutoff, on quiet days as well as on days with a full booking list.

tasks.altitude: The cook still walks the stores and still places the order. A suggested requisition is ready before the walk. No new right to bind the restaurant to a supplier contract.

reach.task: Set pars and supplier cutoff times
reach.learn: Which suggested lines the cook rejected after the storage count.

evidence.claim: Bookings and a par level can suggest a quantity. The cook still has to count the shelf, because waste and a special are not in the history. Model knowledge.
No Annex III point covers costing, menus or food records.
A hygiene app or a waste camera that logs who did what observes staff behaviour and needs works-council consent.

assumptions: The booking list holds date, service and covers. The supervisor or the reservations role produces it. A paper diary is read by hand inside the first step, and that time stays there.
Par levels hold item, unit and target quantity. The cook produces a change to a par only when a recipe changes. Missing history stops the suggestion for that item.
The sent order stores item, quantity, supplier and date. It does not store a score of the cook, and it is not a record of who was on shift.
The cook may send an order inside the standing supplier terms. A new contract or a spend above the cook's limit is a purchasing task, not this one.
Upkeep is correcting a par level. There is no separate admin baseline.
unknowns: Whether bookings at this site are a system list or a paper diary at the pass.
What share of orders are still a phone call to a supplier with no order form.
research_questions: How often a par level is wrong because a special sold a line out.
Whether the cook may send an order with no supervisor, and up to what amount.

already_counted.description: Check the cover count against the booking list before the suggestion is used.
Glance at the suggested quantities and drop a line with no history.
Confirm the sent order matches the quantities the cook decided.

incremental.description: Correct a par level when a recipe change makes the target wrong.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A week of walk-in covers with no booking list, so the suggestion is ignored and the cook still counts every shelf before phoning the supplier.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Consult supervisory staff to plan menus for cost and events.

steps.what: Gather costs and the special event needs
Draft menus from house recipes, costs and event needs

loop.purpose: Draft a short list of menus from house recipes for the named event.
loop.input: The event note, the cost cap, excluded allergens and the house recipe list.
loop.output: Menu options, each with dish, cost and allergen flags taken from the recipe.
loop.check: Code rejects a dish over the cost cap, with an excluded allergen, or repeated inside the set window. The cook rejects a dish the event note does not call for.
loop.stop: No house recipes are linked, three drafts fail the rules, or the cook rejects the list.
loop.why_not_simpler: The event note is free text and mixes guest count, diet and occasion, so a fixed template cannot tell which house recipes fit.

steps.what: Consult supervisory staff about the menus
Agree the menus the supervisory staff chose

tasks.design: House recipes in {DOCS} carry a dish cost from {ERP}. A draft list of menus is checked against the cost cap, excluded allergens and the event note. The cook still consults the kitchen supervisor, who agrees the menus. The draft is not the allergen statement guests see.
tasks.previous_blocker: The event is often described only in the room, and the cost of a dish sat in a spreadsheet the supervisor did not have open.
tasks.enabler_now: A house recipe can show its cost and its allergens, and a draft can be checked against a written cap before the consult.
tasks.still_hard: The consult is where the occasion, the room and the kitchen's week are weighed, and a draft cannot hold that talk.
tasks.human_edge: Judging, with the supervisor, whether a dish fits this event even when the rules pass.

ambition.what: Whether a house recipe stays under the cost cap for this event, before the consult, including small events that now arrive with only a spoken note.

tasks.altitude: The cook still sits with the supervisor and still plans the menus in that talk. A costed draft is on the table when the event note is text. The cook gains no right to publish an allergen claim.

reach.task: Agree the menus for a special event
reach.learn: Which drafted dish failed the cost cap or the event note.

evidence.claim: Recipes linked to supplier prices let a dish cost follow a price change.
Allergen information for non-prepacked food is mandatory, and the operator remains responsible for its accuracy.
A person's diet can reveal health or religion, which is special-category data.
No Annex III point covers costing, menus or food records.

assumptions: The event note holds occasion, date, guest count, cost cap and excluded allergens as dish rules. The supervisor produces it. A spoken-only brief stops the draft, and the consult then starts from the house recipe list.
The note does not hold a named guest's health or religion. A named person's diet is a separate record with its own basis, not this draft.
Allergen flags come from the recipe's ingredients. The cook rejects a flag the recipe does not support. The agreed menus are not the guest-facing allergen statement.
Test the recipe record's own cost field before custom code. A recipe with no cost is shown as missing, not guessed.
Upkeep is relinking a recipe when its cost or allergen data changes. There is no separate admin baseline.
unknowns: Whether event notes at this site name a guest's diet or only a dish rule.
How often the consult happens with no written brief at all.
research_questions: How often a drafted menu is rejected in the consult.
Who is accountable for the allergen statement once a menu is printed.

already_counted.description: Check the event cost notes name the cap and the excluded allergens.
Reject a drafted dish the event note does not call for.

incremental.description: Relink a recipe when its cost or its allergen flags change.

approvals.approved_version: consulted menu options with dish, cost and allergen flags

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A month of events described only in the room, so the draft is empty and the consult still takes the whole meeting.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan menu items and set a selling price from food cost.

steps.what: Open recipe quantities and the supplier price for menu items
Calculate the food cost and price inputs for the items
Choose the menu items and the selling price
Record the selling price against the menu items

tasks.design: Recipe quantities in {DOCS} and supplier prices in {ERP} calculate a food cost per item. The cook still chooses the menu items and the selling price. The price is recorded on the menu list in {DOCS}. This task does not publish the price to guests.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supplier prices arrived on paper or in a mail, and the food cost was reworked in a spreadsheet when a price changed.
tasks.enabler_now: A recipe with quantities and a supplier price can recalculate food cost when the price changes. The selling price stays the cook's choice.
tasks.still_hard: What the room will pay, and whether a dish belongs on the menu, is not a cost percentage.
tasks.human_edge: Setting a selling price the room will accept, using the food cost without being bound by it.

ambition.what: Whether a dish still meets its food-cost target after a supplier price change, including dishes that are not on this month's menu review.

tasks.altitude: The cook still chooses the items and the selling price. The food cost is ready when a supplier price changes. No new right to publish the menu or to change a supplier contract.

reach.task: Accept the selling price onto the guest menu
reach.learn: Which item's food cost moved after a supplier price change.

evidence.claim: Recipes linked to supplier prices let a dish cost follow a price change. The source covers costing a menu item, not choosing the selling price.
The selling price is still a person's choice. A calculated food cost does not know what the room will pay. Model knowledge.
No Annex III point covers costing, menus or food records.

assumptions: The recipe holds item, quantity, unit and yield. The supplier price holds item, unit price and date. Purchasing or the invoice feed produces the price. A paper invoice is typed once into the price field, and that time stays in the open step.
A missing yield or a missing price leaves the food cost blank. It is not estimated.
The recorded price is an internal menu list. Putting it on a guest-facing menu, and any allergen statement beside it, is a later task.
Test the recipe record's own price link before custom code.
Upkeep is correcting a supplier price that does not match the invoice. There is no separate admin baseline.
unknowns: Whether supplier prices arrive as a file or only on a paper invoice.
Who may change a selling price once it is on the internal menu list.
research_questions: How often a recipe has no yield, so the food cost cannot be calculated.
How often the restaurant manager, rather than the cook, sets the selling price.

already_counted.description: Check the opened price is the current supplier price for that item.
Check a blank food cost is a missing yield or price, not a zero.
Check the recorded price is the selling price the cook chose.

incremental.description: Correct a supplier price on the recipe when it does not match the invoice.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: A season of paper invoices, where only repeat items have a price on the recipe and the rest of the food cost is still worked by hand.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The cook still counts the stores, still talks the menu through with the supervisor, and still sets the selling price. A suggested order and a dish cost are ready before those choices. No new right to publish an allergen claim or to change a supplier contract.
reach: Kitchen supervisor: which suggested order lines and which drafted dishes were rejected.
Restaurant manager: which item's food cost moved after a supplier price change.
skills_to_grow: Reject a suggested order the shelf does not support
Reject a menu option the event note does not call for
Set a selling price from the food cost without treating the cost as the price
role.ambitious_version: Each morning the cook sees a suggested requisition and still walks the stores before ordering. Before a menu consult, dish costs and a checked draft are on the table. A supplier price change shows the new food cost, and the cook still sets the selling price.
